beats.text: The Dreaming is still mending around her, but the library stands, and on its far wall one of the three new doors has begun to rattle, as if someone were knocking from the other side.

At her wake they sang the oldest song for the dead: if ever thou gavest hosen or shoon, the fire shall never make thee shrink. The Dreaming kept her anyway, the way it keeps every dream it is not ready to lose.
Daniel, the new Dream, in white, finds her among the shelves. You always wanted to know, he says, what it is like to be one of them. One life. No idea how it ends.
Her realm is ash, and she has forever. The nightmares she can no longer hold drift out into the waking world, and one of them has found a sleeper in London.

She walked away from the Dreaming years ago, and has a life now: a flat over a bakery, an office off the Strand, a fiancée called Jessica, and a name nobody questions. Some nights she dreams of a library, and a door.

She keeps everything, and she will never change. So Lucienne brings her the only new thing in the Dreaming: a door that was not on the wall yesterday. A queen who will never change, Lucienne says, can still read.
Lucienne's report: a dream has come in from the waking world that belongs to no one here. A sewer. A boar the size of an ox. A spear, in a hand that is not quite a hand.
In the dream, a librarian she half remembers reads her a report: a sewer, a boar the size of an ox, a spear in a hand that is not quite a hand.
Someone in London dreams it every night and never reaches the end. A dream that nobody finishes becomes a door.
It is her nightmare. She will have to go in and fetch it back.
Among the carved doors, a plain London street door: peeling black paint, a brass letterbox, the Underground roundel worn into the wood.

To walk a dream from the inside, the Queen of Dreams has to become its dreamer: one woman, one life, an office off the Strand, and a name, Aurie Mayhew. She will not remember being anything else until the story ends.
She does not have to become anyone. She already is Aurie Mayhew. She has only to remember to open the door.
Lucienne: mind the stairs, my lady. They move. And if it goes wrong in there, you will only wake. Your sister will see to that.
The door opens, and the rain comes in, and the warm noise of a pub.

0.3.title: The umbrella

beats.card: A small Scottish town · the night before London

beats.text: Aurie, sick at her own leaving party, shivers on the kerb clutching a rolled-up white umbrella, her friends' gift. A beaky old woman in shawls reads her palm and blinks: not any London I know. It starts with doors.

choices.text: Run after her with the umbrella.

aftermath.text: She clicks the umbrella open and it blossoms into the whole Underground, every line a colour. The old woman wraps herself round it: a good heart is sometimes enough. She wobbles off into the rain, a round white shape spelling Earl's Court, Blackfriars, Angel.

0.3.source: story map 1.1 · novel prologue, pp. 3 to 6

beats.text: Under London a girl has run for four days and sleeps at last in a stone burrow. Somewhere behind her, two gentlemen in elegant black suits send their canary ahead: huge, hairless Mr Ross.
A rat crosses the tunnel. Mr Vandemar's knife flies thirty feet and pins it; he eats it head first, and Mr Croup slaps it out of his hand. People to damage, Mr Vandemar.
Ross tears the rags off her; his knife catches her arm. She lays her hand on his chest and opens him. Croup and Vandemar wait in the tunnel; she knees Croup and runs, bleeding.
Cornered at a blank wall, she prays to the Temple, the Arch, anyone, somewhere safe, and puts her hand to the brick.

1.2.title: Door on the pavement

beats.text: Friday, half past six, off the Strand: trolls ring the monitor, the Wandsworth report is late, and a yellow Post-it on Jessica's photo says tonight. Dinner with her boss. Aurie forgot.
Hurrying to the restaurant, Aurie stops to drop a coin to an old man in a doorway with a yellow-grey beard. There isn't time, says Jessica.
Ahead of them a door opens in a high brick wall. A girl steps out, sways for one long terrible moment, and folds onto the pavement.

Jessica steps over her. Aurie kneels; blood on her fingertips. The girl's eyes open, white in a smudge of dust and blood: not a hospital, they'll find me. Jessica: dial 999, don't give your name, we'll be late.

aftermath.text: Aurie lifts her; she is surprisingly light. Put that girl down, says Jessica, or this engagement is at an end. Aurie walks on and leaves her on the pavement in tears. At the flat the keys lie inside; the girl touches the door, and it swings open.

1.2.source: story map 1.2 · novel ch. 1, pp. 10 to 22

1.3.title: Midnight

beats.text: The ambulance never came. Walking home alone at midnight, Aurie finds the girl still lying there, seen by no one. She carries her home after all.

1.3.source: story map 1.2b · novel ch. 1, pp. 10 to 22

2.1.title: Whose barony is this?
2.1.episodeTitle: Chapter 2 · Two gentlemen at the door

beats.text: The first Beast dream: a sewer, a boar the size of an ox, a spear in a hand that is furred and clawed, the charge, face down in bloody water.
Morning. The girl, in layers of filthy velvet and lace, stares at the buses: I'm in London Above. They bandage her arm at the sink.

canon: Door is hurt, grateful and guarded; she will not go to a hospital or the police.
Most of the blood was someone else's.
Nothing here reveals who she is beyond her first name, which she gives only after the two gentlemen have been.
conversation.opening: London Above. I asked for somewhere safe.

exits.2.1.A: Aurie helps without asking who she is.
exits.2.1.B: Aurie insists on a doctor and the police.
exits.2.1.C: Aurie makes a joke of the whole thing.

choices.text: You need a doctor. And the police.

2.1.source: story map 1.3 · novel ch. 2, pp. 23 to 25

2.2.title: Two gentlemen at the door

beats.text: Mr Croup, small and orange-haired, and Mr Vandemar, huge, in black suits cut two centuries wrong, with posters: HAVE YOU SEEN THIS GIRL? Croup's smile arrives a fraction late.
Vandemar sniffs, walks straight to the bathroom. It is spotlessly empty.
Vandemar, sniffing the air: we heard of a man who dreams of waking. Nasty.

canon: They want the girl, alive. They are polite until they are not.
Croup cuts the phone line whatever Aurie says.
The girl is hiding and can hear everything.
conversation.opening: CROUP: Good morning, madam. We are looking for our sister. Doreen. A troubled child.

exits.2.2.A: Aurie says she has not seen her.
exits.2.2.B: Aurie threatens them with the police.
exits.2.2.C: Aurie glances at the bathroom and gives the girl away.

aftermath.text: Jessica's message on the machine ends the engagement. The girl is making tea. I'm Door.
Croup cuts the phone line anyway. Later: Jessica's message, and a girl making tea. I'm Door.

choices.text: She was here. In the bathroom.
choices.remembered: Door heard that. So did Mr Croup.

aftermath.text: They find nothing, and leave. Then the girl is simply there in the kitchen, making tea, and does not look at Aurie for a long time. I'm Door.

2.3.title: Breadcrumbs

beats.text: Door ties a note to a pigeon with Aurie's blue rubber band: find the marquis de Carabas.
Something bigger than a mouse darts from the videotapes; Aurie flings the remote at it. Door whistles it back: a rat, carrying a brown-paper reply tied on with the same blue rubber band.

choices.text: Apologise to the rat. With dignity.

3.1.title: Orme Passage

beats.text: An alley that should not exist under one gas jet. Aurie turns three times widdershins and tosses the note at a bin; a pile of rags stands up and catches it.

The rags become the marquis de Carabas: a huge dandyish black coat, half frock coat, half trench coat, high black boots, rags beneath, eyes burning white in a very dark face. De Carabas, at your service.

canon: The marquis trades in favours and never answers a question directly.
He will help Door for a favour; what Aurie offers shapes how much he trusts her.
He shoves Aurie down onto the cobbles first and asks the questions himself.
Door's family have been killed; Door wants an escort home and a bodyguard.
conversation.opening: And what, exactly, is the lady Door offering me?

exits.3.1.A: A favour. A really big one.
exits.3.1.B: She'll owe you. So will I.
exits.3.1.C: Aurie bluffs that Door can pay.

3.2.title: The ladder

beats.text: He lifts a manhole with a little metal key and lights a scarlet flare. No questions, no buts: he will hide Door until the Floating Market, two days from now.

Rusted rungs in total darkness, then daylight: the same ladder climbs the outside of a tower a thousand feet up, though it was dusk a moment ago. Above her the marquis lets go with both hands and waggles his fingers.

aftermath.text: On the roof Old Bailey offers starling stew; the marquis forces a silver box on him. A broom cupboard lets them out in Aurie's own stairwell.
He gives none, but he waits. On the roof Old Bailey offers starling stew; the marquis forces a silver box on him. A broom cupboard lets them out in Aurie's own stairwell.

3.2.source: story map 1.6b · novel ch. 2, pp. 33 to 41

3.3.title: Goodbye

beats.text: Door, washed, her short hair shining dark auburn and copper, in a huge leather flying jacket. The marquis kneels: my lady. She kisses Aurie's cheek as friends do and says sorry without saying for what. When Aurie looks up, nobody is there.

3.3.source: story map 1.7 · novel ch. 2, pp. 41 to 42

4.1.title: The Monday nobody sees

beats.text: Monday. On the Tube her sleeve catches in the closing doors; the train drags her along the platform until the cloth tears and she falls. Nobody looks.
Taxis glide past her raised hand. Coins fall straight through the ticket machine. In the office her desk is being carried out, and Sylvia asks politely: and you are?
Only one person in London looks straight at her: a man outside the White Horse, who has drunk in that pub since 1389. He raises his glass. I know you, he says, puzzled. From somewhere.
Jessica's mirrored tower, Angels over England posters. Aurie says she is sorry, not for what she did, but for upsetting her. Jessica apologises for her dreadful memory for faces.

aftermath.text: She calls after her: Aurie... Maybury?

choices.text: I'm sorry I upset you. I'd stop for her again.

4.2.title: The flat is let

beats.text: Through the bathroom door, from the bath: a young agent in a camel coat and a middle-aged couple. The woman runs a finger along the sink. We'll take it.
The phone. Through static, Mr Croup asks whether she knows what her own liver tastes like.

canon: Croup knows she does not know where Door is; he rings to threaten her: they know where she lives, and they make a promise.
The operator cannot hear Aurie if she dials the police.
conversation.opening: Do you know what your own liver tastes like, Mistress Mayhew? Because it's one of the things we could find out together.

exits.4.2.A: Aurie says she does not know where Door is.
exits.4.2.B: Aurie offers to help them find Door.
exits.4.2.C: Aurie says she is calling the police.

beats.text: Croup, delighted: twice helpful, Mistress Mayhew. Vandemar: we don't need the other one. The line goes dead; the flat door opens on its own.
Her sister is waiting, in black, a silver ankh at her throat. You don't die in a dream, little sister, Death says. You wake. Go back, and choose better.
Her sister is waiting, in black, a silver ankh at her throat. You did this properly once, Death says. This isn't that. Go back.
Giving her away once was weakness. Twice was a contract, and they collect. The story goes back to the two gentlemen at the door.

4.4.title: The cash machine

beats.text: Jeans, trainers, her thick black sweater. Into a black sports bag: socks, passport, wallet, fruit from the bowl. You knew, she tells the empty flat. You knew this would happen.
The card is rejected. Aurie gives it to a short old homeless man: fifteen hundred in there, if you can get to it. He hands it back. He can see her.
He has a yellow-grey beard; she gave him a coin once. Have you heard of the Floating Market? A girl called Door? He backs away.

aftermath.text: Iliaster hisses her back and leads her down basement steps.

choices.text: Grab his sleeve. Where is the Floating Market?

4.4.source: story map 2.3 · novel ch. 3, pp. 51 to 53

4.5.title: The bench

beats.text: He flees. Aurie sleeps on a bench.
Near dawn a rat leads her to the same basement door.
Near dawn Iliaster comes back, grumbling, and leads her to the basement door after all.

5.1.title: Cutaway · The closed hospital

beats.text: In a sub-cellar of rot and dripping water, Vandemar drives his knife through his own hand into the plaster. That's how it's done.
Croup takes the call on a Bakelite phone and cringes: the employer wants the Door girl alive.
Vandemar spits on the wound, and it closes.
If you cut us, do we not bleed? Vandemar thinks about it in the dark. No.

5.2.title: The Lord Rat-speaker

beats.text: A vaulted hall of greasy fires and spits. A glass dagger at her throat, a thin girl tipping out her bag, and across the hall people drop flat as a small black rat comes on: the one she threw the remote at. It seems to wink.

canon: The Rat-speaker serves Master Longtail and will do what the rat decides.
Aurie's bag is taken whatever she does; a girl is ordered to guide her to the market.
conversation.opening: Upworlder. You are in the hall of the Rat-speakers, and you will explain yourself to Master Longtail, or you will not.

exits.5.2.A: Aurie greets the rat and asks it about Door.
exits.5.2.B: Aurie kneels with everyone and waits.
exits.5.2.C: Aurie grabs for the glass dagger.

choices.text: Hello, Ratty. Do you know where Door is?

aftermath.text: Horror in the room, amusement in the rat. The bag goes; a thin girl is told to guide her to the market.
Longtail hesitates a moment too long, and the glass leaves a thin red line under her jaw.
The bag goes; a thin girl is told to guide her to the market.

5.4.title: Cutaway · The House Without Doors

beats.text: Before dawn, a boarded door in a misty court; Door takes the marquis's hand and it falls into darkness. Inside, a white hall hung with pictures of rooms, and the walls remember: her brother floating in a Victorian pool, her mother and sister watering plants until Croup steps in.
Her father's study. The marquis pockets a small obsidian beast from the desk.
The marquis snaps open Lord Portico's gold watch and fastens it to his own waistcoat. He's not using it any more.

The journal machine: a cabinet of walnut, brass and prisms. Lord Portico, bleeding, on its little screen: go to Islington. Trust Islington. Avenge us. He steps out of frame, and blood arcs across the white wall.
Elsewhere, Croup and Vandemar hire Varney by pulling his morning-star apart link by link.

5.4.source: story map c3 · novel pp. 60 to 75

6.1.title: Anaesthesia

beats.text: By the hall's spits the thin girl, a stained badge on her rags reading I AM 11, finishes Aurie's last banana. Do you like cat? Thigh or breast?
A bench on the Embankment, the city's lights doubled in the Thames and the Albert Bridge strung with tiny white lights. Quartz beads at the girl's throat. Nobody ever gets both.
And where is this nasty neighbourhood? Knightsbridge. Aurie laughs, and the girl turns away: I said you'd laugh.

canon: Anaesthesia tells her own history in her own words, over a still two-shot; nothing is shown.
She is taking Aurie to the Floating Market by way of Night's Bridge.
conversation.opening: You don't eat much, do you? I ate your fruit. Was that wrong?

exits.6.1.A: Aurie asks about her, and listens.
exits.6.1.B: Aurie talks about her own job and fiancée.
exits.6.1.C: Aurie promises to get her back up here one day.

choices.text: Tell me about you. I'm listening.
Talk about your job and your fiancée.
I'll get you back up here one day. I promise.

6.1.source: story map 2.5 · novel ch. 4, pp. 60 to 71

6.2.title: Night's Bridge

beats.text: Varney's gang shoves Aurie down; Anaesthesia hisses like a cornered rat and Varney backs off, spits at her shoes and leads his gang over the bridge first. A tall woman in mottled leather joins them. Anaesthesia puts the candle-lamp in Aurie's hand.

A stone bridge over a void, no sky and no water. The dark is turned up until it touches the skin. Jessica's contempt; a labyrinth; a spear; the Beast charging slowly out of the black. Anaesthesia's hand shakes in hers. The candle flares so bright it hurts.
From somewhere, a song she cannot place: from Brig o' Dread when thou may'st pass, every night and all.
They sang it at her wake. She does not know how she knows that.

choices.text: Hold her hand tighter and keep walking.
Let go to shield your face.
Call her name into the dark.

6.2.source: story map 2.6 · novel ch. 4, pp. 75 to 80

6.3.title: The beads

beats.text: Nobody is holding her hand. Beads patter down the bridge. The woman in leather: the bridge takes its toll.

choices.text: Go back onto the bridge for her.

aftermath.text: The woman hauls her back by the collar; the beads roll into the dark.

6.3.source: story map 2.6b · novel ch. 4, pp. 75 to 80

beats.text: She let go in the dark and would not look back for the beads. The bridge takes its toll, and tonight it takes two. The woman in leather walks on alone.
Her sister is waiting, in black, a silver ankh at her throat. You don't die in a dream, little sister, Death says. You wake. Go back, and choose better.
Her sister is waiting, in black, a silver ankh at her throat. You did this properly once, Death says. This isn't that. Go back.
The story goes back to the Embankment, and Anaesthesia.

Knightsbridge. Her blank watch goes in a bin. In Harrods' Egyptian Room colour and light break over her: dream sellers, a man in armour selling lost property, a dentist with a hand drill. The woman in leather says fare you well and slips into the crowd.
OLD BAILEY'S BIRDS AND INFORMATION. The feathered old roof-man knows her from the rooftops, and knows where Door is. What'll you give me?

aftermath.text: He waves the handkerchief like a flag and points to the Food Halls: they're auditioning.
Nothing for nothing, he says. She finds the way herself, too late for the first bouts.

beats.text: On the way to the Food Halls five pale sisters sweep past in heavy velvet; the last, the palest, in thin white linen, smiles at her.
The Fish and Meat Hall, sawdust. Bodyguards fight by knack; a thrown Ruislip lands on Aurie.
Late, she pushes into the ring of spectators as a bout ends, and a thrown fighter lands on her.
She opens her eyes on fire-opal eyes in a pale, furious face. Temple and Arch. What are you doing here?

canon: Door is angry because Aurie is in danger because of her; she is kneeling over Aurie on the sawdust.
The bodyguard auditions are still going on; Hunter has not arrived yet. The marquis is here.
conversation.opening: Why did you have to come here? Why couldn't you just stay where you were safe?

exits.7.3.A: Aurie says she did not have much choice.
exits.7.3.B: Aurie says she came to find her.
exits.7.3.C: Aurie says Door knew this would happen to her.

choices.text: I didn't really have much choice.
You knew this would happen to me.

beats.text: A tall woman in mottled leather walks into the ring and puts Varney down with his own blade. I'm called Hunter. The Hunter? I'm back.
Varney staggers up, snatches the crowbar and hurls it at Hunter's head; she simply reaches out a hand and catches it.
A Black Friar tolls a brass bell. The market packs itself away; they come out into a wet, empty street.
The marquis explains the two Londons: Aurie has fallen through the cracks. Good night. She follows down the ladder. Go away. No. They leave her.

aftermath.text: The water rushes on toward East London. Alone in the dark, for the first time since her father died, Aurie cries.

beats.text: She keeps their lamp in sight through two tunnels, then loses it at a fork and sits down in the dark.

8.3.title: Cutaway · 259 stairs

beats.text: Varney flees down a spiral stair, two hundred and fifty-nine steps. At the bottom the lift doors slide open with magnificent slowness: Vandemar on the bottom step, paring his nails with Varney's machete. Croup falls on him from above.
In a tunnel Door stops: we can't leave her. The marquis: of course we can; we did. Door, too tired for patience: you are working for me, aren't you?

8.3.source: story map c5 · novel pp. 96 to 98

beats.text: A ledge above a storm drain. Her lamp finds Aurie. She says sorry, and means it.

canon: Door came back for her against the marquis's advice.
They are looking for an angel named Islington.
Door can promise to try to get Aurie home, not more.
conversation.opening: I'm sorry. I shouldn't have left you. Are you coming?

exits.8.4.A: Aurie says she has nowhere else to be.
exits.8.4.B: Aurie will come only if Door gets her home.
exits.8.4.C: Aurie says no, and Door sits beside her in silence until she asks again.

choices.text: Only if you get me home.

aftermath.text: She promises, carefully. They are looking for an angel. Aurie laughs until it echoes.
Door sits beside her in silence. After a while she asks again, and this time Aurie gets up.

beats.text: A rock hall, iron pillars running off into the dark, a waterfall into a rock pool, a black door of flint and silver. Candles wake as a small barefoot woman in white passes; she kneels at the pool, drinks, closes her eyes. No wings, but unmistakably an angel: Islington.

9.1.title: No such things as angels

beats.text: Hunter: there are shepherds in Shepherd's Bush; pray you never meet them. In the Bank tunnel the busker Lear can see them; the marquis buys his train schedule with a pennywhistle reel that sets passers-by tossing coins onto Lear's coat.
He taps Angel on the Tube map: Islington. Aurie has heard enough about angels.

choices.text: There are no such things as angels.

9.1.source: story map 4.1 · novel ch. 6, pp. 101 to 105

9.2.title: Mind the gap

beats.text: A Central Line platform. Hunter: mind the gap. Black smoke wells over the edge.

choices.text: Step back when Hunter warns you.

aftermath.text: The smoke snaps at nothing. Door holds her hand while she shakes.
It wraps her ankle; Hunter beats it off. Her jeans bleach where it touched; purple welts. Door holds her hand while she shakes.

9.2.source: story map 4.2 · novel ch. 6, pp. 105 to 107

9.3.title: Cutaway · Scarecrows

beats.text: The hospital courtyard of junk and frogs. The employer's orders: scare her, not kill her. Crows overhead: a murder.

9.3.source: story map c7 · novel pp. 107 to 109

9.4.title: The court on the train

beats.text: On the platform one carriage stands dark and locked. The marquis knocks; the door slides open six inches on firelight and smoke, and an old bespectacled face peers out.

Through the glass the carriage is dark and empty; inside the door, firelight. Straw, chickens, a wolfhound, old men-at-arms in knitted chain mail. The huge one-eyed earl shuffles in, in a fur dressing gown and carpet slippers.
The earl surges up, his head brushing the roof. De Carabas cost him a dozen men and an eye in the retreat from White City. Two ancient guards level crossbows at the marquis.
At a stop an old man-at-arms raps a vending machine: orders from the earl. It spits chocolate bars into his helmet.

canon: The earl holds an old grudge against the marquis (the White City retreat, his eye).
Door can invoke her house; the marquis leaves at the next station either way.
Tooley the jester calls Aurie a mooncalf; the earl does not.
conversation.opening: I know you, de Carabas. I may be old, but I haven't forgotten. Who brought him into my court?

exits.9.4.B: Aurie speaks up for the marquis.
exits.9.4.C: Aurie agrees the marquis seems dodgy.

choices.text: Say nothing. Let Door handle it.
He's with us. Leave him be.

14.1.title: The Ordeal

beats.text: BLACKFRIARS. An empty platform, a lonely mausoleum, newspaper pages skittering onto the rails. Then light and noise hit like a bottle: rush hour. Posters: GIVE UP. YOU WERE NEVER THERE.
Gary sits down: I'm not really here. I'm you. His face runs like putty into her own.
In the train window she sees herself: filthy, black-eyed, a street sleeper. Jessica, who is also her, cries that she had a breakdown.

Gary tosses her the purple-haired troll from her old desk; it falls through her hands. She crawls after it through the crowd; someone stamps on her fingers; an old woman's foot knocks it into the gap. It lies by the third rail.
Her hand finds the bead, and she hears Anaesthesia: Aurie. Hold on.
In the dark she hears Anaesthesia's voice, small and clear: you let go.
Hunter's voice, from somewhere: mind the gap.
An old woman's voice: you've a good heart.

canon: The other Aurie insists she has had a breakdown and has been wandering; she is persuasive.
The train that comes carries the lost from the wall of faces.
Climbing down after the troll is the end.

beats.text: A dark, silent hall. Door alone, one wrist chained, a candle. It is done, without them.

20.3.title: The angel's hall

beats.text: Door chained spread-eagled, a bruise on her cheek. Come in, Aurie Mayhew. You do look a mess.
Croup's fist; then Vandemar bends back her little finger until it snaps. Croup brings in the marquis: you told me he was dead. He was. The mask slips.
Key, door and opener, the angel explains, must be the three. Portico laughed at it, so it had him killed. Lucifer was an idiot. And then, mildly: not all of you, of course.
Atlantis drowning, four million voices; Islington waking and calling Croup through the rock pool.
They deserved it, she screams, and for one moment the sweet face is something else entirely. Then, mildly: just one of those things.
Vandemar recites Portico's real words in his voice: Door, child, fear Islington. A blade under Aurie's ear.
You asked nothing for yourself, she says. Then your pain is your gift to Door.

canon: Islington wants Door to open the flint door; she will hurt Aurie to make her.

If BARGAIN_SELF: she offers Aurie her life back if Aurie tells Door to open it. If BARGAIN_DOOR: she mocks that Aurie's pain is her gift to Door. If BARGAIN_ATLANTIS: she knows Aurie knows about the city.
She never raises her voice until she screams that they deserved it.
conversation.opening: Tell her to open it, Aurie Mayhew. And I keep my word: your life back. Every bit of it.

exits.20.3.A: Aurie tells Door not to open it; they don't matter.
exits.20.3.B: Aurie begs Door to open it.
exits.20.3.C: Aurie accuses it of sinking a city and calling it unfortunate.

choices.text: Don't do it, Door. We don't matter.

effectsIf.ripple: You asked nothing for yourself, and still ask nothing.

aftermath.text: The marquis, on his knees: actually, I matter very much.

choices.text: You sank a city and called it unfortunate.

20.3.source: story map 8.4a · novel ch. 17, pp. 236 to 246

20.4.title: Jam tomorrow

beats.text: Door: stop them, I'll open it. Her palm on the flint until a keyhole appears, throwing laser-white light. The angel whispers to the killers: when I am gone, kill them all, howsoever you wish.

choices.text: To the killers: you don't think you'll ever see her again, do you?

aftermath.text: They mean to collect, in full, with interest and meat hooks. Jam tomorrow.

choices.text: I've sat across a table from Lucifer. I've met better angels than you. Worse ones too.

aftermath.text: Croup and Vandemar look at the angel, then at each other. They mean to be paid, in full, with interest and meat hooks.

20.4.source: story map 8.4b · novel ch. 17, pp. 236 to 246

20.5.title: The false door

beats.text: The door opens on churning orange and purple; candles, then the table, fly into it. Gravity, not wind. That's not Heaven. What have you done?
It was Hammersmith's copy; she opened a door as far and hard away as she could. Islington offers news of her living sister, and falls into the light.
Croup climbs Vandemar's back, boasting that he killed her family; the old suit tears. Bye-bye, says Vandemar, and lets go. The door slams.
Somewhere a long way down, two gentlemen in black suits go to collect, in full, with interest and meat hooks.
Darkness. Door frees them; Aurie holds her; the marquis, afraid of sleep now, sleeps last.

20.5.source: story map 8.4c · novel ch. 17, pp. 236 to 246

20.6.title: The true door

beats.text: The real key opens on quiet gold light. Islington steps forward. The killers seize her robe for their pay.

aftermath.text: She slams the true door on the struggle. Islington stays imprisoned; Croup and Vandemar walk out unpaid.
Unpaid, Croup and Vandemar spit at the angel's feet and walk out. Islington sits alone among her candles, a prisoner again, until the friars come with lanterns.

20.6.source: story map 8.4d · novel ch. 17, pp. 236 to 246

beats.text: Behind her, Vandemar draws his knife: kill them all, howsoever you wish. The angel walks into true light, promising to reward the worthy and cast down the hateful. The abbot: we have lost the key; God help us all.
Her sister is waiting, in black, a silver ankh at her throat. You don't die in a dream, little sister, Death says. You wake. Go back, and choose better.
Her sister is waiting, in black, a silver ankh at her throat. You did this properly once, Death says. This isn't that. Go back.
In Lucienne's library a locked door shivers. The story goes back to the market on HMS Belfast, where the key could still have been lent.

21.1.title: The friars' table

beats.text: In the labyrinth, a towering woman in white boots and a torn lace train lifts Hunter's body and the spear, and carries them away.
Aurie wakes in a grey robe, finger splinted, ear stitched. Door in a robe far too big, reading Mansfield Park; the marquis wheeled in like a swashbuckler. Hunter? There was no body.
You are the Warrior, the abbot says.

She slipped the real key into Aurie's pocket at the market. The abbot: you are all very stupid people. The key is the key to all reality; Aurie is its master until she returns it; it will take her home.
The friars took the real key back from the hall. The abbot: you are all very stupid people. You held it; you are its master until you return it; it will take you home.

canon: The key will take Aurie home; whoever turns it, she remains its master until she returns it.
Door and the marquis are at the table and may speak.
conversation.opening: You are all very stupid people. And you are the master of the key, until you give it back. Well?

exits.21.1.A: Aurie asks when they could do this.
exits.21.1.B: Aurie asks what happens to London Below first.
exits.21.1.C: Aurie gives the key back and says she is staying.

choices.text: Not yet. What happens to London Below?

21.1.source: story map 8.5 · novel ch. 19, pp. 248 to 252

21.2.title: Nightingale Lane

beats.text: A ghost station reached from the friars' bell tower. Old Bailey waves Aurie's own handkerchief on a stick, me little flag, and gives her a black feather bound with red thread.
The feather, Old Bailey says, came off a talking bird who works for a lady who dreams.
She has said she is staying; Door sends her to be honoured all the same.
A ghost station reached from the friars' bell tower. Old Bailey gives her a black feather bound with red thread.
The earl's train, a ragged fanfare: thought you'd be taller. Knighted with Hunter's knife: Lady Aurie of Maybury, the freedom of the Underside.
The earl's train. Tooley: the one who was with the Hunter. Knighted all the same, with Hunter's knife.
The earl's train. Knighted with Tooley's bauble, which is what there is.
Somewhere below, two gentlemen in black suits walk away unpaid.
At a gloaming terminus the Lord Rat-speaker returns the bag: no hard feelings about Anaesthesia; the rats are your friends.
In an underpass the Velvets watch from the shadows, and Lamia blows her a kiss.

aftermath.text: Sometimes they do.

21.2.source: story map 8.6 · novel ch. 19, pp. 252 to 256

21.3.title: The island of Westminster

beats.text: A frosted hill at dawn above a wide clean river, two smaller rivers running into it: London three thousand years ago. Door in new brocade under the old jacket. There's sorting out to do and only her to do it; her sister may be alive. Please don't go.
I promised to get you home, she says. I keep my promises.

canon: Door asks Aurie to stay; she will turn the key for her if she goes.
If KEY_RETURNED, Aurie has already given the key back and said she is staying.
conversation.opening: Please don't go. I mean, I know you have to. But please don't.

exits.21.3.A: Aurie says she has to go home.
exits.21.3.B: Aurie stays (earned by loyalty and their bond).
exits.21.3.B2: Aurie stays, as she already said at the friars' table.
exits.21.3.C: Aurie takes the key and turns it herself.

aftermath.text: She turns the key in the air: just walk, don't look back. Aurie looks back; Door's cheeks are wet.

choices.text: I said I'm staying. I meant it.
Take the key and turn it yourself.

aftermath.text: Then go.

21.3.source: story map 8.7 · novel ch. 19, pp. 256 to 258

22.1.title: London Above

beats.text: Trafalgar Square, an October morning: a sticky child says this woman is bothering her. Aurie grins and runs through the pigeons, and they burst up around her.
The cash machine works; a taxi stops; A. MAYHEW, JUNIOR PARTNER on a door; the penthouse of unpacked cases. Nights at the dark window.
Hunter's knife on the mantelpiece.
Jessica, with the ring: perhaps one day Aurie would give it back to her.

choices.text: You keep it. I'm sorry. I've just changed.

choices.remembered: Something up here holds you now.

22.1.source: story map 8.8 · novel ch. 20, pp. 259 to 266

22.2.title: A rat on the bins

beats.text: A brown rat on the bins behind Newton Mansions, cleaning its whiskers as if it owns the world. Across the road the Buchanans watch her.

22.2.source: story map 8.8b · novel ch. 20, pp. 259 to 266

22.3.title: Are you coming?

beats.text: A Friday night out with the new girl from Computer Services; Aurie sees the rest of her life laid out: wedding, children, Croydon. Not a bad life.
A Friday in the pub, then Gary finds her outside; in a greasy spoon she tells him everything. The people who fall through the cracks freeze in doorways on the Strand, he says.
On Windmill Street, the black feather in her pocket.

choices.text: Drop the feather in the gutter.

22.3.source: story map 8.9 · novel ch. 20, pp. 267 to 273

22.4.title: The wall

beats.text: Gary puts her in a taxi: this is reality; get used to it. She gets out at the next corner.
When she walks back, the feather is gone from the gutter.
Ten pounds to an old woman asleep in a doorway, a once-white umbrella tied to her wrist; the faded Tube lines still show.
Ten pounds to an old woman asleep in a doorway, a dirty umbrella tied to her wrist.
If this is all there is, she doesn't want to be sane. She draws Hunter's knife at a brick wall off Brewer Street.
If this is all there is, she doesn't want to be sane. A brick wall off Brewer Street, and nothing in her hands.

canon: Gary believes she has been ill; he is kind about it.
Nothing he says changes the exits, which are taken alone at the wall.
conversation.opening: So. London Below. Rat-speakers. An angel. You do know how that sounds, right? Get in the taxi, Aurie.

exits.22.4.A: Aurie cuts a door in the brick with Hunter's knife and hammers on it.
exits.22.4.B: Aurie takes the next taxi home.

choices.text: Cut a door in the brick with Hunter's knife. One across, two down.

22.4.source: story map 8.9b · novel ch. 20, pp. 267 to 273

beats.text: The outline becomes a hole in the wall. The marquis, arms folded, yawns. Well? Are you coming?
She touches the feather in her pocket, and goes.
They walk through, leaving not even the doorway.
The bricks swing open from the other side: Door, chin up, asks the same question. The marquis lurks behind her.
She touches the feather in her pocket, and goes.
They walk through, leaving not even the doorway.

23.3.title: Ending B · Lady of the Underside

beats.text: She never goes up. The next Floating Market: Aurie helping Door broker peace between baronies; Old Bailey waving his little flag.
At the edge of the crowd, a rat-speaker girl who might be Anaesthesia.
Hunter's name, carved on the giants' gate.

23.4.title: Ending C · Get used to it

beats.text: Nothing opens. Dawn on the pavement.
The penthouse; the cases unpacked at last, the girl from Computer Services helping.
The knife in a drawer.
Lucienne: it is not a bad life. It is just not hers.
Aurie wakes in the reading chair. In her hand, a silver key on a thread.
Lucienne shelves the book beside the Sandman. There is room on the shelf for two more.
You forgave the one who sold you, Lucienne says. That was very like you, my lady.
Daniel is waiting by the shelf. He wants to hear all of it.
